01.reason: A certain person came before Rav Yosef, who ruled and was challenged by Abaye: a narrated incident resolved by a ruling.

02.reason: Eyewitness account of a woman coming before Ameimar, the brothers' response and his silence: a real incident with a reaction, cited as evidence.

03.reason: A halakhic exchange between Rava bar Rav Hanan and Abaye; speech only, no narrated event.

04.reason: A remedy plus a one-line report of a goat with no spleen, cited as corroboration; nothing follows.

05.reason: The death of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi: the decree, the maidservant's prayer and jug, bar Kappara's announcement; a full narrative.

06.reason: A get is found in Rav Huna's court, Rav Huna rules, Rav Hisda sends Rabba to investigate and he finds the source: an incident with actions and a response.

07.reason: Orphans come before Rava, he rules, the Sages challenge him and he justifies it: incident followed by a ruling.

08.reason: The Sidon tanner incident with the Sages' ruling is a story, though it is the Mishnah's own copy (R-C1).

09.reason: A woman writes her property to her daughter, marries and is divorced: the opening of a narrated incident with several actions.

10.reason: Orphans come before Rava, he rules, the Sages challenge him and he justifies it: incident followed by a ruling.

11.reason: Funeral costs drove relatives to flee; Rabban Gamliel had himself buried in linen and everyone followed: a one-time act with a response and a change.

12.reason: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi tricks the Angel of Death, jumps into paradise and meets Rabbi Shimon ben Yohai: a full narrative.

13.reason: A remedy plus a bare one-line report that Rav Shimi bar Ashi used it and the patient was healed, cited as evidence.

14.reason: A man has ten write a get, the signing is delayed, he comes before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, who rules: incident plus ruling.

15.reason: Wondrous incidents (the mustard branch breaks, nine kav found, its wood used for a booth) narrated as events; the eyewitness-wonder type he has accepted.

16.reason: A man sets a 30-day get condition, is held up by the ferry, shouts across the river, and Shmuel rules: incident plus ruling.

17.reason: A habitual practice (the maidservants would sing to Rabbi Abbahu) with no one-time event following.

18.reason: Rabbi Hanina declines the appointment, Rabbi Afes dies, Levi goes to Babylonia and Rav deduces it: a narrative chain of events.

19.reason: Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba meets Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi hurrying his grandson to school, asks why, and changes his own practice from then on.

20.reason: Ulla dies abroad, they tell Rabbi Elazar, he laments, they say the coffin is coming, he answers: an event with responses.

21.reason: Rabba bar bar Hana brings a partly unwitnessed get and comes before Rabbi Elazar, who rules: incident plus ruling.

22.reason: A yevama case set up as an incident, but the passage is mostly negotiation between the brothers: speech with conflict and no resolution in the passage.

23.reason: A legal discussion of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel on nursing vows; no narrated event.

24.reason: A legal ruling with an incident only alluded to in one line (a woman strangled her child) as evidence; not narrated.

25.reason: A man makes a deal with his sharecropper, rain comes, and Rav Yosef and Rabba rule: incident plus ruling.
